surprises.head: Nikita Tolopilo stole one
surprises.body: Tolopilo allowed 2 goals on 36 shots, worth 5.9 expected goals: 3.9 fewer than expected. That is more than Vancouver’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 450 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

surprises.head: Vancouver won against the run of play
surprises.body: With chances like these, Utah would win about 71 games in 100. Vancouver won anyway.

story.head: Tolopilo robs the Mammoth in Utah
paras: Jake DeBrusk struck first for the Canucks on the power play late in the second. It was a busy third period. Vincent Trocheck tied it up for Utah on the power play early in the period, and Filip Chytil restored the Canucks’ lead just under two minutes later. Barrett Hayton tied it 2-2 for Utah midway through the period, but that was the last goal the Mammoth would get. Brock Boeser put the Canucks ahead for good on the power play with less than five minutes left. He finished with a goal and two assists.

The Mammoth will be kicking themselves: they had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Mammoth win about seven in ten. Nikita Tolopilo made the difference in net, stopping 34 of 36. The Mammoth hit two posts and still lost. Karel Vejmelka stopped 21 of 24 for the Mammoth.

The officials called 14 penalties, a total the league sees about once every 40 games. The Canucks moved to 5-17-1, still last in the NHL, while the Mammoth dropped to 10-9-3, slipping to sixth in the Central.

items.text: The Mammoth are winless in six (0-3-3).
Brock Boeser has a point in eight straight games.
Clayton Keller extended his point streak against Vancouver to seven games.

The Mammoth were without Nate Schmidt, John Marino, Nick Schmaltz and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche were missing more at the time.
